title: IDF Sniper Kills Food-Seeker in Jabalia Camp; 8-Year-Old Found Dead After Northwest Gaza Strikes; Naval Fire Wounds Fishermen
detail: On Day 957 of the Gaza war (May 25, 2026), IDF sniper fire killed Samih Dardouna, 23, near a clinic in Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza. A relative told reporters Dardouna was 'looking for food to feed his displaced children' at the time of the shooting. Separately, the body of 8-year-old Hani Abdullah Shakshak was recovered from a tent in the Al Tuwam area of northwest Gaza following overnight Israeli airstrikes. Israeli naval vessels fired heavy machine-gun rounds toward Palestinian fishermen off Gaza's coast, wounding three. The IDF also confirmed on May 25 that its May 24 Nuseirat strike targeted Mohammad Abu Mallouh — identified as a senior Hamas technical expert in weapons production who had used the ceasefire to manufacture new weapons. The IDF carried out controlled demolitions of residential structures in eastern Khan Younis, Gaza City, and northwest Gaza.

media.caption: Hani Abdullah Shakshak, 8, killed after Israeli airstrikes in northwest Gaza — May 25, 2026

title: Five European Nations Ban Ben-Gvir; Italy Formally Requests EU Sanctions Over Flotilla Activist Mistreatment
detail: The diplomatic fallout from Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's treatment of detained Global Sumud Flotilla activists escalated sharply on Day 957 (May 25, 2026). Spain, the Netherlands, and Belgium joined France and Poland in banning Ben-Gvir from their territories, creating the widest diplomatic censure of a sitting Israeli minister in modern history. Italy formally requested the European Union weigh bloc-wide sanctions on Ben-Gvir, backed by France, Ireland, and Spain. Italy, France, the Netherlands, Poland, and Canada all summoned their Israeli ambassadors. TIME magazine's May 25 report documented the European bloc's consolidated response. Israeli FM Gideon Sa'ar publicly stated Ben-Gvir had caused 'serious diplomatic harm' to Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu called Ben-Gvir's conduct 'not in line with Israel's values' but defended Israel's right to intercept the flotilla. Spanish police detained four returning flotilla activists at Bilbao airport following clashes. Eight Arab and Islamic nations — UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Jordan, Qatar, Turkey, Indonesia, and Pakistan — issued a joint statement condemning Ben-Gvir's actions. EU-level sanctions require unanimous agreement of all 27 member states.

media.caption: Five European nations ban Israeli minister Ben-Gvir as diplomatic crisis deepens over flotilla — May 25, 2026

title: Netanyahu Accused of Stalling Ceasefire to Time Gaza Offensive With Domestic Elections
detail: Al Jazeera reported on May 25, 2026 that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is deliberately prolonging ceasefire negotiations and intensifying military operations in Gaza in alignment with the timing of upcoming domestic elections. The report draws a direct link between the escalation of Israeli offensive activity and Netanyahu's political calendar, with critics accusing him of prioritizing electoral considerations over a deal that could end the conflict. The accusation comes as Israel has increased strikes across Gaza and as ceasefire talks mediated by Qatar, Egypt, and the United States remain deadlocked. Opposition figures and international observers have warned that Netanyahu's government has used the war to suppress domestic political pressure from coalition partners, particularly the far-right bloc led by Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who have threatened to collapse the government if any ceasefire deal is reached.

media.caption: Netanyahu accused of stalling Gaza ceasefire negotiations ahead of domestic elections — May 25, 2026

title: Gaza Encircled by Famine: Only 44% of Daily Flour Needs Reaching Territory; Medicine Critically Low
detail: A May 25, 2026 report documented Gaza's deepening food and medicine crisis on Day 957: the territory requires approximately 450 tonnes of flour per day but is receiving only about 200 tonnes, causing bakeries to shut down and long queues to form with little or no bread. Medicine stocks are critically low across all hospitals in Gaza, endangering thousands of patients. Restrictions on generators, engine oil, and spare parts are causing system failures in health, sanitation, and debris removal infrastructure. UN OCHA's May 15 Humanitarian Situation Report documented that only 69% of aid supplies from Egypt were successfully offloaded in the first 11 days of May 2026. The 111 community kitchens produce 1.1 million meals per day — below the 1.25 million needed. The 2026 UN Humanitarian Flash Appeal of $4.1 billion remains only 12% funded ($540M received), with $3.6 billion still unmet. UNRWA has been blocked by Israeli authorities from directly bringing personnel and aid into the Gaza Strip since March 2025.

media.caption: Gaza's food and medicine supply crisis: only 44% of flour needs and critically low medicine stocks — May 25, 2026
